questions.stem: What does textual ETL do with raw text?
options: It reads text, disambiguates it and places the words found, together with their context, into a structured database
It compresses documents to save storage space
It translates text into other languages
It converts structured tables into free-form prose
It deletes documents that contain no numbers
questions.explanation: Textual ETL reads and disambiguates text, capturing each selected word and its context as the data is placed into a structured format.

questions.stem: How does textual ETL know which words to pluck out of text?
options: It selects the most frequently occurring words
By fiat of one or more taxonomies that flag which words are important and provide their context
A systems programmer hard-codes each word
It chooses words at random
It extracts only words that appear in capital letters
questions.explanation: Taxonomies alert textual ETL as to which words are important enough to be placed in a database and also provide the context for the selected word.

questions.stem: What is inline contextualisation in textual ETL?
options: Translating each word into a numeric code
Attaching document metadata to every row
Selecting a word and its context by its position in the raw text and its proximity to other words and phrases
Sorting words alphabetically before loading
Summarising a document into a single sentence
questions.explanation: Inline contextualisation handles words that taxonomies cannot, using the word's position in the raw text and its proximity to other words and phrases.

questions.stem: What is the key difference between structured data and textual data illustrated by the $5000 bank deposit and the phrase 'I like biscuits'?
options: Structured data is larger than textual data
Textual data is always older than structured data
Structured data is stored in files while text is stored in databases
Structured data is precise whereas textual data is probabilistic
Textual data cannot be stored in a database
questions.explanation: A $5000 deposit is an exact amount, but 'I like biscuits' can be interpreted in several ways, showing that structured data is precise while textual data is probabilistic.

questions.stem: What is needed before analytics can be run across both structured data and textual data together?
options: A second data warehouse
A licence for each document
A dedicated systems programmer
Deleting the structured data first
Some common connector between the two types of data
questions.explanation: Analytics on structured data alone or textual data alone is possible, but analytics against both requires some common connector of data.

questions.stem: What is the document card catalogue used for in a corporation?
options: Quickly and efficiently finding corporate documents, including documents that relate to each other
Recording employee attendance
Storing customer credit card details
Listing which books employees have borrowed
Logging server performance
questions.explanation: Like a library's card catalogue, the document card catalogue helps a corporation find its documents and discover which documents relate to each other.

questions.stem: Roughly what proportion of the data in a corporation is estimated to be text?
options: 50% exactly
Less than 1%
questions.explanation: It is estimated that 85% to 95% of the data in the corporation is comprised of text, and nearly all of it is untouched by today's analysts.

questions.stem: In the real-estate example of textual ETL, how are the words 'owner' in one document and 'trustee' in another treated?
options: They are stored in separate databases
The word 'trustee' is discarded as a duplicate
They are recorded as the same data because their logical meaning is the same, even though the text differs
They are flagged as a conflict for a consultant to resolve
Only the more frequent word is kept
questions.explanation: Textual ETL groups data by its logical meaning, not its physical manifestation, so 'owner' and 'trustee' are recorded as the same data.

questions.stem: What distinguishes the word column of a textual ETL database from the name column of a standard database?
options: The word column is always empty
The word column holds only numbers
The word column can hold only a single word per document
The word column is heterogeneous, holding any kind of word found in the document, whereas the name column is homogeneous
The word column is defined by metadata before any document is read
questions.explanation: In a standard database every element of the name column is a name, but the word column of a textual ETL database is heterogeneous and free to hold any kind of word.

questions.stem: In a textual ETL database, what does the classification (or context) column contain?
options: The file size of the source document
The date on which the document was loaded
The name of the analyst who ran the process
The number of times a word appears
The classification that gives meaning to the word in the same row, such as 'flu' being a disease or 'Eliquis' a medication
questions.explanation: The classification column gives meaning or context to the word in the same row, so the metadata of the word is contained in the database structure itself.
